Let $\alpha = e\left(i\dfrac{2\pi}{10}\right) = e^{i\dfrac{\pi}{5}}$

Now, $z^{10} - 1 = ( z - 1 ) ( z - \alpha ) \ldots \left(z - {\alpha}^{9}\right) \ldots. ( 1 )$
so $, {ℓ}_{1}{ℓ}_{2} \ldots {ℓ}_{9} = | 1 - \alpha | \left|1 - {\alpha}^{2}\right| \ldots \left|1 - {\alpha}^{9}\right|$

$| z | = 1$

$⇒ z^{n} = e^{i2k\pi}; k \in I$

$z = 1, $e\dfrac{i2\pi}{n}, e\dfrac{i4\pi}{n}, \ldots , e\dfrac{i2\left(n - 1\right)\pi}{n}

All roots$ of unity lie on arc of circle.

questions.solution:
It is given that complex numbers $z = x + iy and w = u + iv$ are on the unit circle such that $z^{2} + w^{2} = 1 . . . ( i )$

So, $\overset{¯}{z^{2}} + \overset{¯}{w^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ \left(\overset{¯}{z}\right)2 + \left(\overset{¯}{w}\right)2 = 1$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\overset{¯}{z}z}{z}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{\overset{¯}{w}w}{w}\right)2 = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{z2} + \dfrac{1}{w2} = 1 ⇒ z^{2} + w^{2} = z^{2}w^{2}$

 $⇒ z^{2}w^{2} = 1 . . . ( ii )$

$∵$ The number of solution of equations $x^{2} + y^{2} = 1 and x^{2}y^{2} = 1$ is eight 

$∴$ Number of ordered pair $\left(z, w\right)$ is also eight.
